paper_id: Novel Artificial Bee Colony Algorithms for QoS-Aware Service Selection
title: Novel Artificial Bee Colony Algorithms for QoS-Aware Service Selection
motivation: Population-based algorithms for service selection are too complex to configure; existing ABC variants use generic neighborhood search that behaves like random search in discrete space.
problem_framing: Formulate QoS-aware service selection as NP-hard discrete optimization with large search space; need to adapt ABC from continuous to discrete domain while preserving its simplicity advantage.
key_insight: Continuous ABC's success stems from 'optimality continuity' property (similar variables yield similar function values); discrete ABC lacks this because neighborhood covers entire solution space; approximating this property via QoS-similarity-based neighbors improves convergence.
method_signature: Three algorithms (IBA/PBA/EBA) achieve approximate optimality continuity through ratio-based, partition-based, and experience-based neighborhood definitions respectively.
evaluation_criteria: Solution accuracy and convergence speed compared against ProHR and GDE3; ablation of individual/partition/experience techniques.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: New parameters (R, C, H) require tuning; approximation may exclude some qualified neighbors; combinations of algorithms not thoroughly tested.
evidence_for_taste: the neighborhood search of the discrete ABC is quite similar to a random search
existing population-based algorithms ... are often poor at exploitation
the former makes it difficult to leverage the unique characteristics of SSP
poorly-configured parameters could lead to undesirable QoS
the complexity of finding all the qualified neighbors is comparable with that of the SSP
thinking_moves: Identify root cause: discrete ABC neighborhood Eq.(8) covers entire solution space, losing local search property
Borrow 'optimality continuity' concept from continuous optimization as theoretical anchor
Map continuous neighborhood structure analogy to justify discrete approximation
Realize not all qualified neighbors need to be reachable (Table 2 shows even continuous functions miss qualified neighbors)
Derive three complementary implementations from same principle but different mechanisms
